chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, all from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A woman left behind her husband, her brothers (from mother), and her sisters (from father). He said: 'For the husband is half (three shares), and for the brothers from the mother is one-third, male and female are equal in it, and one share remains for the brothers and sisters from the father: "For the male is like the portion of two females."'

Because the shares do not increase (in number of heirs to reduce share) and the husband is not reduced from the half, nor the brothers from the mother from their third, because Allah, Exalted and Mighty, says: 'If there are more than that, then they are partners in the third.'
And if she is one, then for her is one-sixth.

And what Allah meant [by Kalalah]: 'And if a man or woman leaves no descendant but has a brother or sister, then for each one of them is one-sixth. If there are more than that, then they are partners in the third.'
He meant by that specifically the brothers and sisters from the mother.
And He said at the end of Surah Al-Nisa: 'They ask you for a legal ruling. Say: Allah gives you a legal ruling concerning Kalalah. If a man dies leaving no child, and he has a sister...'
Meaning a sister from mother and father, or a sister from father. 'Then for her is half of what he left, and he inherits her if she has no child.'
And if they are brothers, men and women, then for the male is like the portion of two females.
These are the ones who are added to and reduced from, and likewise their children who are added to and reduced from.

And if a woman left her husband, her brothers from her mother, and her two sisters from her father, then for the husband is half (three shares), and for the brothers from the mother are two shares, and one share remains, which is for the two sisters from the father.
And if there was one, it is for her, because if the two sisters were two sisters from the father, they would not be increased beyond what remains.

And if there was one, or if in place of the one there was a brother, he would not be increased beyond what remains, and a female from the sisters or from the children is not increased beyond what a male would not be increased upon.

key_terms.اَلْإِخْوَةُ مِنَ اَلْأُمِّ: Brothers and sisters from the mother (full or half)
key_terms.اَلْكَلَالَة: A person who leaves no direct descendants or ascendants
key_terms.لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ اَلْأُنْثَيَيْنِ: For the male is the portion of two females

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed when a woman leaves behind a husband, maternal siblings, and paternal siblings?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the inheritance distribution for a deceased woman leaving a husband, maternal siblings, and paternal siblings, citing Quranic verses to justify the fixed shares of the husband (half) and maternal siblings (one-third). He clarifies that the remaining share goes to paternal siblings with the male receiving double the female, emphasizing the principle that these specific shares do not reduce (ta'wil) even when multiple heirs are present, a nuance derived from the concept of Kalalah.
